open_points.subject: backup snapshot/write concurrency
open_points.text: Its read transaction and the store's writes do not wait for each other... No change or run is refused or fails for the other.
open_points.question: Which module owns and enforces the new non-blocking, mutual-nonfailure contract between the backup read transaction and store writes? `store` owns SQLite transactions and the snapshot mechanism, but its section names only snapshot consistency; under the decision-allocation rule the unnamed remainder of A18 belongs to `backups`, which cannot enforce SQLite write/read interaction without depending on an unowned `store` guarantee.
options: `store` owns the non-blocking snapshot/write contract and `backups` consumes it
`backups` owns the contract and is allowed to control the store transaction mechanism needed to enforce it
open_points.default_guess: Make the non-blocking snapshot/write behavior part of `store.copy_store_snapshot`'s owned contract, consumed by `backups`.
